title: OpenAI puts Pro subscriptions on hold due to Astra demand
snippet: The company said Pro subscriptions put the most strain on its systems, so it's pausing sign-ups while adding more capacity.
fullText:
Demand for OpenAI’s newest and most powerful model, Astra, has led the company to temporarily pause subscriptions for its $200-per-month Pro plan, citing strain on its infrastructure.

The move was announced on X by OpenAI’s product leader, Thibault (Tibo) Sottiaux, who leads core products like Codex and ChatGPT at the AI lab. He said that the Pro plan puts the most strain on its systems, which is why sign-ups for this service tier are now being disabled.

“We wanted to take the smallest step that allows us to continue giving the broadest access possible,” Sottiaux wrote. He added that the company’s other plans, including the API and lower-cost Go and Plus plans, remain available.

The company warned on Wednesday that such a change might come. At the time, Sottiaux wrote, “Demand for Astra is really unprecedented. We’re pulling all the levers possible to sustain the demand, but I’ve not seen anything like it until now and we went through very steep growth before. Priority will always be to keep excellent service for existing users, but we might have to pause new Pro subscriptions for a bit if this continues.”

OpenAI hasn’t said how long sign-ups to the Pro tier may be disabled, or how many people are signing up daily, to give an idea of the scale of the demand.

The company raised usage limits for Codex users as recently as last month, suggesting the strain is a recent phenomenon.

Launched on September 3, Astra has been rolling out across OpenAI’s plans, including Pro, Plus, Enterprise, and Business accounts, in addition to its AI. The model promises a major leap forward in areas like AI reasoning, coding, and computer use — all areas of steep competition. OpenAI even heralded Astra as the beginning of the “AGI era,” and a generational leap, stoking demand even more.

title: You Can Now Buy the Trump Phone for $250 More Than Originally Priced
snippet: Trump Mobile’s T1 phone now costs $749, echoing price hikes across other phone retailers.
fullText:
After Apple’s Surprise and Shine event on Wednesday, which debuted the long-rumored foldable iPhone Duo with a starting price of $1,999, the conversation at my home has mainly centered on our mobile phone expenses and whether it’s worth upgrading.

Well, good news: There is a flashy phone on the market that is cheaper than the hyped-up foldable. OK, there are many well below that price, but do they operate on an outdated operating system? Are they painted gold?

Ring the alarms and throw the confetti; I am talking about Trump Mobile’s golden T1 Phone.

Read more: Trump Mobile and its T1 Phone Don’t Make Any Sense, Even for Trump Fans

The gold-colored mobile device was originally priced at an affordable $499. Due to a quiet price hike the provider implemented overnight, as first reported by The Verge, the Trump phone is now marked at $749. That’s a $250 increase, making the T1 a more expensive option over the iPhone 17E. Control your excitement.

A Trump Mobile spokesperson didn’t immediately reply to our request for comment.

Trump Mobile didn’t explain the cost increase, but the writing has been on the wall for some time. The company’s execs went on record earlier this year with The Verge that the initial $499 price tag was a temporary introductory price. It’s even possible for the T1 to become more expensive, with a price of up to $999 in the future. So, you know, embrace this price while you can.

That said, the company didn’t provide any firm explanation beyond that, leading us to speculate that this could be due to the ongoing global memory chip shortage driven by the AI boom, known as RAMageddon. Apple recently implemented an array of price hikes due to the RAM shortage, upping the price of its older iPhone lineup, iPads, MacBooks and more.

But the Trump phone isn’t in the same ballpark as an iPhone. In fact, the Trump phone is essentially a reskinned mid-level HTC handset.

This might be the worst possible shade of gold.

Corinne Reichert/CNET

After an almost year-long delay, the Android phone, originally advertised as made in the US, began shipping in May to members of the media, which included CNET (you can read the full review here), along with a few customers (who paid a preorder deposit of $100 for the device).

Once CNET’s experts were able to take a closer look at the T1, which is now labeled as being “assembled in the USA,” we confirmed what iFixit learned before us: The Trump phone was likely manufactured in Guangdong, China, and is nearly identical to the Taiwanese HTC U24 Pro. The latter handset was released to market two years ago and can be found for less than $600 at retailers such as Walmart and Amazon.

But are those HTC handsets I mentioned above painted gold? Do they come equipped with Truth Social on an outdated OS, while their casings are decorated with an American flag missing some stripes? I think not. 

So, if you’re still in the market for Trump Mobile’s T1 phone, I advise you to get while the getting’s good. Before we know it, the Trump phone could be priced at around $1,000. I’m all for retro tech and nostalgia, but for all the outdated tech this phone is built on, that price tag is pushing it when newer phones on the market, sporting more impressive bells and whistles, are clocking in at a price that’s way lower.

title: iOS 27 launches next week: Here are three new features I’ve been loving
snippet: iOS 27 is packed with new features across Messages, Notes, Apple Wallet, CarPlay, and more. Here are three of my favorite new iOS 27 features. more…
fullText:
iOS 27 is packed with new features across Messages, Notes, Apple Wallet, CarPlay, and more. Here are three of my favorite new iOS 27 features.

#1: Siri app

Siri is completely new in iOS 27, rebuilt from the ground up for the AI era. And one exciting upgrade is the dedicated Siri app. Per Apple:

When users want to revisit a past conversation or kick off a new one, they can open the all-new dedicated Siri app. The Siri app uses iCloud to privately sync conversational history across a user’s products, so they can start chatting with Siri on Mac and continue the conversation on iPhone, iPad, Apple Watch, or Apple Vision Pro, bringing together rich conversations in one place.

The Siri app provides a convenient, go-to home for any question you have. It’s especially great for chatbot-style conversations that go beyond a simple request.

With the popularity of apps like ChatGPT, Claude, and Google Gemini, a dedicated Siri app makes a lot of sense. And since it’s pre-installed on the iPhone Home Screen, I suspect it could quickly become a go-to app for many users.

#2: One-tap suggestions in Messages

iOS 27 has plenty of Apple Intelligence features that don’t “feel like AI” but simply offer convenient tools. One shining example is actionable suggestions in the Messages app. Per Apple:

Messages offers one-tap suggestions based on the context of users’ conversations, making it easier than ever to get things done, such as creating a reminder or a note. For example, if someone asks for photos, Messages can also help users find the right ones, recognizing keywords, locations, and people in their library to find the best options.

Plenty of messaging apps have tried to infuse AI via an integrated chatbot in your conversation. I’ve never been a fan of that approach. 

But one-tap suggestions in Messages offer similar utility in many respects, and are quicker and easier to use than typing out an AI request. It’s the kind of AI feature I can fully get behind.

Note: Apple announced today that suggestions won’t launch in iOS 27.0, but instead have been pushed to a future update.

#3: ‘Smart Event Details’ in Apple Calendar

Apple’s Calendar app gets a new feature in iOS 27 that I’ve long wanted: natural language input for creating events. Apple calls it ‘Smart Event Details.’

Using Apple Intelligence, you can type out an event in your own words and have iOS 27 automatically detect and fill in key details, including:

title

time

location

invitees

With Smart Event Details, you won’t need to manually enter these details separately anymore. Instead, you can just type everything in a single line, and AI will update your event accordingly.

title: Is It Me or Is the iPhone Duo Looking More Like the All-in-One Device?
snippet: Getting rid of another device or two might make Apple’s $1,999 foldable phone worth it.
fullText:
Before now, Apple really didn’t have a device that sat between an iPhone and an iPad to give you a bigger screen while still being a smartphone. But is Apple’s first foldable phone all you need now? 

CNET Senior Tech Reporter Abrar Al-Heeti says the new iPhone Duo resembles a passport, with a 7.6-inch display inside and a 5.4-inch display outside. But how much smaller is it compared to Apple’s tiniest tablet? 

By comparison, the iPad Mini is bigger than the iPhone Duo, with a screen size of just over 8 inches. But the iPhone Duo’s functionality and bigger screen size make me wonder if it’s the perfect handheld device if you’re already considering a new iPhone and iPad. 

CNET Director of Content Patrick Holland previously told me a foldable phone, like Samsung’s Z Fold lineup and Galaxy Tab series, is a niche product and isn’t meant to replace the iPhone model you may be used to. But it makes me wonder if the iPhone Duo is Apple’s way of selling to those who want one device to do the work of two. Especially if you’re already considering upgrading your personal devices ahead of the holidays.

	

			

Let’s do the math.

Say you’re eyeing the iPhone 17 base model (256GB), which now starts at $899. But maybe you want an iPad with more power and speed for other tasks, so you pick the iPad Pro, which starts at $1,199. Boom. You’ve already spent $99 more than the $1,999 iPhone Duo. 

Or maybe you want the iPhone 18 Pro Max (256GB) for $1,299 and the iPad Mini for $599 — totaling $1,898. That’s $101 less than the Duo’s starting price, but the extra money may be worth it if you want the convenience of having one device instead of two. Especially since the iPhone Duo is packed with features and specs like Dual Capture to FaceTime on the front and rear cameras simultaneously. The ultrawide and main cameras are both 48 megapixels, and it has a powerful battery that gives you up to 24 hours of power if you use both displays. And the real bonus is the A20 Pro chip for better speed and performance. Plus, you can still expect all the bells and whistles iOS offers. 

But CNET Editor at Large Scott Stein made a few points in his commentary that you should consider. The iPhone Duo only supports the USB-C Pencil for now, not the Apple Pencil 2 or Pencil Pro. And the foldable doesn’t run on iPadOS. It’s an iOS variant with a different layout, so if you have iPad-specific apps or games, they may not work as intended. 

The CNET team will conduct a full hands-on test of the iPhone Duo soon to evaluate all of the perks and pain points. But take it from me, as someone who has a MacBook Pro, iPad Mini and iPhone 17 Pro Max, I rarely use all of those devices. The iPhone Duo could be one device that suits all of your needs. (Or at least two out of three.) And maybe that’s a new audience that Apple’s hoping to capture.

title: The Crunchyroll and Fox One Bundle Hits Prime Video
snippet: The anime and live sports streaming services come together for a limited time for $23 per month.
fullText:
If you’re a fan of anime and live sports, this news is for you: Sony’s streaming service Crunchyroll has launched a bundle with Fox One for customers based in the US. The package, called the Crunchyroll Fan Tier x Fox One bundle, costs $23 per month and is now available on Prime Video for a limited time.

It’s worth noting that this pair-up offers customers a 23% discount compared to the price for subscribing to each service separately. Crunchyroll on its own costs $10 for its ad-free plan; Fox One costs $20 per month.

Pairing sports and anime fandoms may sound out of place, but a recent study by Crunchyroll from the National Research Group shows how strong the entertainment genre has become. “54% of Gen Z globally make their love for anime known — just behind LeBron James at 59%, and ahead of Serena Williams at 47% and Shohei Ohtani at 25%,” the press release states.

Fox One features a full slate of Fox’s entertainment brands, including Fox News, Fox Sports, the Fox Network, Fox Business, Fox Weather, FS1, FS2, Fox Deportes, the Big Ten Network and your local Fox stations.

Crunchyroll is the largest anime streaming platform in the world, boasting over 21 million subscribers. The service features anime hits like Dragon Ball, Naruto and My Hero Academia, along with current standouts Black Torch, Jaadugar: A Witch in Mongolia, Smoking Behind the Supermarket with You and One Piece Heroines.

This is the second bundle Crunchyroll has launched this year. Earlier this summer, the streaming service announced its first, with Starz. snippet: Frank Shaw in 2025. | Image: Microsoft Frank Shaw is leaving Microsoft after 17 years as chief communications officer. Shaw has been at the heart of Microsoft's communications since 1997, helping the company navigate multiple Windows and Office releases, CEO transitions, the all-important bet on cloud, and huge acquisitions like the $26.2 billion LinkedIn purchase in 2016 and the $69 billion acquisi … Read the full story at The Verge.
fullText:
Frank Shaw is leaving Microsoft after 17 years as chief communications officer. In an internal note to his team, Shaw says he’s “decided it is time for me to move on and try new things,” after supporting Microsoft’s communications for 29 years — nearly 20 years as a Microsoft employee plus time at the Waggener Edstrom agency (now We. Communications) before that.

Shaw has been at the heart of Microsoft’s communications since 1997, helping the company navigate multiple Windows and Office releases, CEO transitions, the all-important bet on cloud, and huge acquisitions like the $26.2 billion LinkedIn purchase in 2016 and the $69 billion acquisition of Activision Blizzard in 2023.

He’s well-respected across the public relations industry, and PRWeek recently named him number one on its 2026 list of the most powerful people in the PR industry. Internally at Microsoft he’s also well-respected among executives, and has built up a reputation for being direct, but respectful. Many employees have told me over the years that they always fear an email from him for misspeaking or accidentally leaking product plans.

He’s earned a reputation outside of the company as someone who is always willing to argue with critics, correct stories, and defend Microsoft. In 2013, he ripped into Apple and the press for daring to compare iWork to Office, and he regularly appears on X to shoot down rumors or to correct information about Microsoft. At Microsoft’s 50th birthday party last year, he appeared onstage to read out a series of hilarious mean tweets about his PR activities.

I’ve been covering Microsoft for more than 25 years, and I first encountered Shaw as a naive teenager trying to get into blogging. I would post confidential Microsoft documents online at my time at Neowin, or blog about early Windows features before the company was ready to announce them. That regularly got me into trouble with Microsoft’s army of lawyers, and even got Neowin knocked offline for 24 hours.

Despite there being a great deal of mutual respect between us, I’ve upset Shaw plenty of times over the decades, leading to some heated debates or disagreements over stories. Still to this day, when Frank calls my phone, I brace myself, knowing Microsoft is either about to announce something crazy or I’ve upset the company again.

But what’s he doing next? Shaw isn’t retiring just yet, but he tells me he’s going to take a well-earned break before moving on to “other things” he wants to do. Could that be PR for an AI startup? Baking sourdough bread professionally? In a manner befitting a communications professional: He refuses to tell me.

Microsoft isn’t naming a replacement for Shaw yet, as he’s not leaving the company until the end of the year. “I’ll be here through the end of the calendar year, and the company is working through next steps, look for an update in the next few weeks,” says Shaw in a note to his team.

Here’s Shaw’s full internal memo to his communications team:

(don’t bury the lede)

After 17 years in this role and nearly 29 working with the company, I’ve decided it is time for me to move on and try new things. Takeshi and I have been talking about this for a while, and I am excited about what’s next, for me and for Microsoft. I remain optimistic about the company mission, the incredible talent on this team, and how much the company depends on us during this critical time. I’ll be here through the end of the calendar year, and the company is working through next steps, look for an update in the next few weeks. I know you will have many questions, and I’m looking forward to talking to you at our AMA here later this morning <link>

(start burying)

A while back, there was a social media trend where people answered the question, “What topic could you give a 30-minute presentation on with no preparation?” Me, I could talk about the US Marines, the changing nature of influence, sourdough starter, the Oregon Ducks, but my go to would have to be aspects of Stephen King’s the Dark Tower books, starting with “The Gunslinger;” the question then becomes which particular aspect. A quick primer, the series follows Roland Deschain, the last of the gunslingers (a mix between mayor/judge/sheriff), as he chases the man in black through time and dimensions in a quest to save the world. The question embedded throughout is if it is possible for Roland to retain his identity and meaning in a world that had moved on. The refrain is that the world moves on, move with it or fall. Can Roland move and grow, or will he be stuck? One of the concepts that sticks with me comes as we are introduced to more characters, now moving with Roland. He introduces the concept of ‘ka-tet’ to describe them. ‘Ka’ is essentially fate, or destiny, and ‘tet’ translates to a group of people, put together for a larger meaning – a group brought together with a shared mission and destiny, a group with shared goals, the willingness to sacrifice for those goals, with a deep emotional connection to each other and the ability to make and act on decisions with what can feel like supernatural speed.

I’ve always loved the evolution from the solo gun slinger we meet in book one to the team that operates throughout the later books. Roland on his own was formidable but failed in his missions, as part of a ka-tet he was in the end successful.

You, my friends, are my ka-tet. Together, we’ve accomplished amazing things. My gratefulness is endless.

We will have time together still over the next set of months as we finalize decisions and deliver great work on behalf of the company, and I will be close by after. In the Dark Tower, the traditional departure saying is “long days and pleasant nights,” and so it will be, but not until December. 😊

title: iOS 27: Here are Apple’s full release notes
snippet: Today Apple announced that iOS 27 will launch next Monday, September 14. Here are the full release notes for the major new iPhone update. more…
fullText:
Today Apple announced that iOS 27 will launch next Monday, September 14. Here are the full release notes for the major new iPhone update.

Apple’s official iOS 27 release notes available now

Apple has published the full iOS 27 release notes as part of its RC update today. They’re included unedited below:

Siri AI (All iPhone 16 models and later, iPhone 15 Pro, iPhone 15 Pro Max)

A more capable and conversational version of Siri is rolling out to users. It helps you find what you need and get more done, drawing on capabilities like personal context understanding, app actions, onscreen awareness, and access to broad world knowledge

New voice experience offers more expressive and natural-sounding voices, and lets you customize expressivity and pace to make Siri more personal to you using powerful on-device models on iPhone Air and iPhone 17 Pro models and later

Dedicated Siri app provides an easy way to revisit an existing conversation or kick off a new one, and privately syncs conversations across your Apple products with iCloud

Siri mode in Camera integrates Visual Intelligence into the Camera app, letting you ask questions and take action with what’s in front of you, like splitting a bill or looking up nutritional info for a plate of food

Write with Siri enables you to generate a draft from scratch, edit what you’ve written, or get feedback from Siri virtually anywhere you type. In Messages & Mail, Siri personalizes your writing style based on your relationships, and uses unique phrases and punctuation that you’ve previously used in your conversations with those people

Apple Intelligence across apps (All iPhone 16 models and later, iPhone 15 Pro, iPhone 15 Pro Max)

Photos

Spatial Reframing lets you adjust the composition of a photo after it was taken by virtually changing the camera position

Extend tool intelligently expands images beyond their edges with realistic infill, so you can straighten horizons, change aspect ratios, or add more space around a subject

Clean Up supports removing even larger objects, with more realistic, high-quality results, and you can choose between Fast mode for small blemishes or High Quality for more intricate edits

Safari

Organize by Topic uses Apple Intelligence to sort your tabs, analyzing webpages and automatically grouping similar tabs together

Notify Me can periodically check a webpage for updates, like price changes and item availability

Describe an Extension lets you create a custom extension using natural language to adjust your view of a website’s content or formatting

All-new Image Playground uses a new generative model to make high-quality images in virtually any style, including photorealistic, lets you modify your images using touch and natural language, and lets you generate Lock Screen wallpapers and Contact Posters with personalized suggestions

Describe a Shortcut lets you use natural language to create a shortcut or refine an existing one

Home

Summarized activity notifications combine related alerts across accessories into a single notification

Video descriptions for HomeKit Secure Video recordings summarize what’s happening in a clip for eligible iCloud+ subscribers

Camera clip search lets you find specific moments from your HomeKit Secure Video cameras by searching in the Home app or Spotlight when on an eligible iCloud+ plan

Describe an event in Calendar lets you use natural language to create an event, and details like the time, location, invitees, and event title are filled in using Apple Intelligence

Suggestions in Mail help you take action based on the context of your emails, like getting directions to a restaurant you booked

Call Context in the Phone app understands when you’re speaking to certain businesses and proactively surfaces relevant information from across your apps, like a confirmation code or a reservation number

Accessibility

VoiceOver enhancements include more detailed and contextual image understanding for photos, charts, and screenshots, a conversational experience that lets you ask questions about your screen or surroundings, and a new way to get answers fast with an Action button integration

An enhanced Magnifier experience offers conversational visual assistance for users with low vision, with a high-contrast interface and natural language app controls for zooming and other Magnifier functions

A smarter Accessibility Reader uses intelligence to provide better text cleanup and formatting, images and tables, on-demand summaries, and translation

Voice Control flexible inputs help you navigate your device with just your voice by describing elements on screen in your own words, like “tap the gear” or “tap the button in the top right”

And more, including additional ways to create and modify Genmoji, automatic proofreading, and more accurate dictation using an on-device model on iPhone Air and iPhone 17 Pro models and later

Child Safety

Improved setup experience for new child accounts lets parents choose the exact apps their kids can access when they set up an iPhone for their child

Ask to Browse gives parents the option to approve each new website before their child can view it

Expanded Communication Safety protections help intervene before children see gore or violent content in shared images and videos

Time Allowances help parents set boundaries around how long kids can use apps across Entertainment, Games, and Social Media apps, offering guidance based on expert research and tailored to each child’s age

Schedules let parents choose which apps their kids can access at different points in their day and across weekdays and weekends

Redesigned Screen Time settings give parents at-a-glance information about how their kids use their devices, and controls to adjust access in just a few taps

System Improvements

Liquid Glass refinements improve overall readability, and a new slider in Settings lets you personalize its appearance from ultra-clear to fully tinted 

Faster performance in experiences across the system, including app launches, new photos loading in your Photos library, and AirDrop transfers

Improved search provides more relevant and comprehensive results in Spotlight, Photos, and Mail

Connectivity Assist enables more seamless transitions between Wi-Fi and cellular networks

And more improvements across apps and experiences, including enhancements to iCloud Shared Albums in Photos, Custom EQ for AirPods, support for perimenopause and menopause in Cycle Tracking in the Health app, and independent volume settings for Alarms and Timers

For information on the security content of Apple software updates, please visit:

https://support.apple.com/100100

Some features may not be available in all regions or on all iPhone models. To learn more, please visit:

https://www.apple.com/ios/feature-availability/

Usage limits may apply for some Apple Intelligence features. To learn more, please visit:

https://www.apple.com/apple-intelligence

Software updates, like this one, add new features and improvements that may affect performance and/or battery life. To learn more, please visit:

https://support.apple.com/125039

fullText:
The iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max are almost here. Announced at Apple’s September 2026 “Sunrise and shine” event alongside the iPhone Duo and other new gear, the two upgraded phones feature the faster A20 Pro processor with more GPU power as well as more neural cores for AI-related tasks, plus some welcome improvements to the camera.

The phones will arrive on Friday, September 18th, and preordering one is never a bad idea if you want to ensure you get the color and storage capacity configuration you’re seeking. Speaking of, preorders are officially open.

The 6.3-inch iPhone 18 Pro starts at $1,199 for the 256GB model, and goes all the way up to $2,399 for the version with 2TB of storage. The larger 6.9-inch iPhone 18 Pro Max starts at $1,299 for 256GB, with the 2TB model costing $2,499. Both phones are available in four colors: deep black, silver, glacier, and burgundy.

At the time of publication, the only way to preorder an unlocked version of the Pro or Pro Max is directly from Apple. You have some options if you don’t want to pay the full price upfront. Financing through Apple is an option (36 monthly payments with zero percent APR), and the new phones are also eligible for the recently-announced Apple Upgrade program. You can also trade in your existing phone for up to $885 in credit towards the cost of the new phone, with carriers offering additional credits.

$1199

The likes of Best Buy and Walmart only have the carrier-locked versions listed at the start of the preorder phase. Best Buy is offering the 18 Pro through Verizon or AT&T, along with the Pro Max tied to Verizon or AT&T. Walmart is offering the 18 Pro through Verizon, AT&T, and T-Mobile, as well as the Pro Max with T-Mobile, Verizon, or AT&T.

Offers from US carriers

AT&T will offer to cover the cost of an iPhone 18 Pro via billing credits paid back to you over 36 months if you trade in an iPhone 14 or newer. You’ll also need to sign up for the AT&T Extra plan, with slightly lower discounts for less expensive plans. You can find these options on Apple’s checkout page, with the option to pay the $99 difference between the Pro and Pro Max out of pocket.

T-Mobile is offering the iPhone 18 Pro for free by way of bill credits when you transfer your number or trade in a qualifying phone on the Experience Beyond plan. The credits aren’t as generous as AT&T’s offer if you’re an existing customer already, with only the iPhone 16 and newer covering the cost of a new phone, but it’s very similar if you’re new to T-Mobile.

The Verizon deal is fairly straightforward. The Simplicity Pro plan, which comes to a total of $80 per month if you’re switching from another carrier, includes a free iPhone 18 Pro, with the option to upgrade your phone after one year. Like other carriers, the “free” phone is paid off to you via monthly bill credits, so you’ll need to stick with the carrier for three years to get the full value.

snippet: Sony has detailed what’s new in its Android 17 update, but only five Xperia phones are going to be getting it as of now. more…
fullText:

title: iPhone 18 Pro vs iPhone 17 Pro: Here’s everything new
snippet: Today Apple unveiled iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, its latest flagship models. Here’s everything new with iPhone 18 Pro vs last year’s iPhone 17 Pro. more…
fullText:
Today Apple unveiled iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, its latest flagship models. Here’s everything new with iPhone 18 Pro vs last year’s iPhone 17 Pro.

Cameras: New 48MP Main camera with variable aperture

Every year Apple makes the iPhone camera system better. But with four different cameras on the iPhone Pro models, sometimes changes are limited to one camera or another. Last year, for example, brought an all-new Center Stage front camera and Telephoto improvements.

With iPhone 18 Pro, the Main camera is the focus of Apple’s upgrades.

Apple says the 48MP Fusion Main camera is all-new, notably adding a variable aperture feature. Here are the details:

The new 48MP Fusion Main camera with variable aperture is the most advanced camera Apple has ever made, bringing aperture control to iPhone for the first time along with even more creative control. Six laser-cut blades smoothly transition between different apertures, making it incredibly easy to capture the best shot by automatically adjusting for depth of field and lighting. Combined with a new sensor that improves image quality, the result is better low-light photography, crisper detail in the back of group photos, and more unique shots. Variable aperture also provides more control for creative pros by giving them the ability to manually adjust any of the four aperture settings in the Camera app, and an API is available to developers for even more control across the aperture range in their apps.

Users will be able to switch between ƒ/1.48, ƒ/1.8, ƒ/2.8, and ƒ/4.0 variable aperture options.

Apple also introduced a variety of new Camera app software features, including updated Photographic Styles and pro controls for lens aperture, shutter speed, white balance, and viewing histogram. Those are all exclusive to iPhone 18 Pro too, as are Smart focus tracking, Cinematic mode effects from video, and Apple Reference Image.

Performance: A20 Pro chip and thermal upgrades

The new A20 Pro chip is a big upgrade over last year’s A19 Pro. That’s partly thanks to the new 2nm process it was built on, which improves performance and efficiency.

A20 Pro has a 6-core CPU, with 2 new super cores that Apple says are the fastest in any smartphone, plus 4 new efficiency cores. There’s also a 7-core GPU with 40% faster graphics performance, increased bandwidth, and faster Neural Accelerators than A19 Pro.

iOS 27 is packed with major AI features, and A20 Pro is an especially big leap for AI. That’s thanks to a new Dual 16-core Neural Engine—that’s double the number of cores as A19 Pro.

Finally, A20 Pro has a 50% increase in memory bandwidth, and thermal performance is improved thanks to a second-generation vapor chamber. Ultimately, these changes lead to 40% improved sustained performance over iPhone 17 Pro.

Design: New colors, uniform rear design, redesigned Dynamic Island

iPhone 18 Pro largely retains the same design as iPhone 17 Pro, with a prominent camera plateau on the back.

The most notable design change involves color. iPhone 18 Pro comes in four new colors: Burgundy, Glacier, Black, and Silver. This gives it a fresh look versus the bold iPhone 17 Pro colors.

Apple has also updated the back of iPhone 18 Pro with a more unified blend of colors between the glass cutout and aluminum frame. Last year’s models had a two-tone design, but this year it’s a more uniform look.

Finally, there’s a redesigned Dynamic Island on the front of iPhone 18 Pro. Its smaller footprint enables up to three simultaneous Live Activities.

Battery: Best-ever battery life, faster charging

iPhone 17 Pro and Pro Max offered the best-ever iPhone battery life. But this year Apple is upping battery life yet again, with big gains especially for iPhone 18 Pro Max.

Battery Life (video playback)

iPhone 18 Pro

up to 36 hours

iPhone 18 Pro Max

up to 45 hours

iPhone 17 Pro

up to 33 hours

iPhone 17 Pro Max

up to 39 hours

Faster wired charging is included with iPhone 18 Pro too, which can get 50% charge in just 15 minutes.

Connectivity: Apple-designed C2 modem on at least 18 Pro

Apple has a new in-house C2 modem debuting in iPhone 18 Pro. It replaces the Qualcomm modem found in iPhone 17 Pro, while still including support for mmWave in the US.

Here are the details via Apple’s press release:

iPhone 18 Pro introduces C2, Apple’s next-generation cellular modem system, which brings AI-powered improvements to cellular quality and reliability. C2 delivers meaningfully faster uploads when compared to C1X while consuming 15 percent less energy, and now supports mmWave in the U.S.

Interestingly, Apple’s tech specs page suggests that C2 might be exclusive to iPhone 18 Pro, with the Pro Max model sticking with Qualcomm.

iPhone 18 Pro vs iPhone 17 Pro: wrap-up

	

iPhone 18 Pro starts at a higher $1,199 price, compared to $1,099 for iPhone 17 Pro. iPhone 18 Pro Max gets a similar $100 increase, starting at $1,299.

fullText:
Today at its September event, Apple unveiled iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Duo, but there was no base model iPhone 18 introduced. Here’s why.

iPhone 18 base model expected to launch in early 2027, as Apple shifts release schedule

Normally, it might be common to refer to today’s Apple event as the “iPhone 18 event.”

But in a move that likely surprised many, Apple didn’t announce an iPhone 18 today—at least not the base model.

Instead, the company debuted three high-end new iPhones only: iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and iPhone Duo.

This flagship lineup differs significantly from Apple’s prior pattern of shipping a new base iPhone at the same time as Pro models. But reporting dating all the way back to May 2025 predicted such a change was coming.

Per widespread reports, Apple’s three new iPhone models introduced today will be joined by three more debuts in early 2027:

iPhone 18

iPhone 18e

iPhone Air 2

So the base iPhone 18 hasn’t been canceled, it’s just shipping later than usual.

Why the change?

One theory is that since Apple wants to expand the iPhone lineup more than ever, with new models like the foldable Duo, it didn’t want to overcrowd the fall. Thus, splitting major iPhone launches into fall and spring cycles might be advantageous.

Another possible reason is that Apple saw the current memory shortage coming, and knew it would be a struggle to meet demand if it launched the base iPhone 18 at the same time as Pro and Duo models.

In any case, the iPhone 18 is still coming—just not until the early months of 2027.

title: Lenovo’s Googlebook 15 Gets a New Specs Leak. Brace Your Wallet for Impact
snippet: Make no mistake: This is not a Chromebook, and it won’t be cheap.
fullText:
Lenovo’s upcoming Googlebook 15 just got its latest and most comprehensive leak, and woof — this is not the affordable Chromebook you’re used to if the specs are accurate. The leak comes from MacObserver, which has the full purported specs sheet, showing that the Lenovo Googlebook 15 is very much going to be a premium laptop, though the leak doesn’t reveal a price or exact launch date.

A Google representative did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Under the hood, we’re apparently looking at an Intel Core Ultra 5 325 processor, 16GB or 32GB of LPDDR5x RAM, 256/512GB storage and a 70-watt-hour battery that can last for up to 11 hours. MacObserver notes that the leaked machine is identified as GB 151PH12, and according to Lenovo’s naming guide, IPH is the platform code for Panther Lake-H, so you can expect an Intel integrated graphics chip.

Google announced the new device in May and said it would go on sale this fall.Google

The laptop sports a 15.3-inch, 2,880-by-1,800-pixel OLED display with a 120Hz refresh rate and a 16:10 aspect ratio with super-thin bezels, according to the leaked photos that you can view on MacObserver. Brightness is 500 nits, and it has 100% DCI-P3 color. According to the leaked specs, the entire device will weigh just 2.84 pounds and measure 13.43 by 9.29 by 0.63 inches. It’s also touchscreen.

Another interesting feature on the laptop’s exterior is the Glowbar, a colored Google indicator on the lid that shows battery and charging status. It’s not clear whether this will have additional functionality like the erstwhile Touchbar on older MacBook models did, but we’d guess that you’re able to customize some of the indicator options.

Googlebooks replace the Windows icon with a G on the keyboard.Google

You get a haptic trackpad (150 by 95 millimeters), fingerprint sensor and Google facial authentication, the company’s challenge to Apple’s Face ID and possibly related to the technology at play with Google Pixel’s Project Toscana. According to the leaked specs, for that purpose, there’s a 5MP RGB webcam with dual microphones and a physical privacy shutter, which is a nice touch.

Audio also seems like it’ll be solid, with four Dolby Atmos speakers that are visible on either side of the keyboard in the leaked renders. Speaking of the keyboard, there appears to be a dedicated Google “G” key on the bottom row between the Function and Alt keys. That could be a command key, similar to what we get on MacBooks, perhaps something that activates AI tool Gemini, which the company has said can provide more proactive help. It should sync well with Android phones, letting you access apps and files directly on the Googlebook, a feature available through Microsoft Phone Link on Windows.

It’s currently unclear from the specs leaks whether there will be deeper integration with Android, whether the new proactive help capabilities will be exclusive to Googlebook or whether they will come to other devices in the future. It will be restricted to certain countries and languages, as well as users who are 18 and older.

The main features of a Googlebook. 

Google

The port loadout looks fairly solid with a Thunderbolt 4 port, USB 3.2 Type-A port and audio jack on the left side. The right features another Thunderbolt 4 port and HDMI 2.0. It comes with Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 5.4. The keyboard is also backlit.

The specs leak also revealed details about accessories expected to accompany the Googlebook. It looks like there may be a bundle that includes the laptop, along with a Lenovo E310 True Wireless Earbuds and a Lenovo 540 Convertible Tote backpack.

There’s also a Lenovo “AI Mouse,” which has the same colorful LED indicator on it as the Googlebook. Details aren’t available about what makes the mouse AI, but it could be similar to what we’ve seen on Logitech’s productivity mice, like the MX Master series, which offer seamless file sharing and cross-device functionality.

Chromebooks captured the budget and midrange laptop segment for non-Apple users, but the idea of a premium Chromebook never really took off due to Chrome OS and its challenges in handling real productivity. The goal of Googlebook is to give you access to the full range of Android apps on your phone, along with storage for files and improved functionality. 

“The basic idea is that using a Googlebook shouldn’t be all too different from using a Chromebook or any other laptop; you’ll just get more Gemini AI-powered tools built in, along with access to the full universe of Android apps,” said Josh Goldman, managing editor for CNET’s computing coverage. 

Goldman notes that the biggest advantage of the Googlebook over Chromebooks is that it can bring features originally developed for Android to the device more quickly, citing Circle to Search as an example. “It took roughly a year for the feature to make the jump from Android phones to Chromebook Plus laptops. But now, an AI feature like Create Your Widget — which lets you quickly generate custom widgets and was only recently announced for Android phones — will also be available on Googlebooks.” 

The only details we’re really missing at this point are the price and exact release date, though a fall launch is expected, so it may be any day now. For price, if we were to take an educated guess, this is not going to be a cheap laptop. With the specs under the hood here, 9to5 Google points out that you’re looking at a device that will likely be priced similarly to Lenovo’s ThinkPad X9 15 Aura Edition, which starts at $1,519 for the base model and upward of $2,396 for a more heavily specced-out unit.

There’s no doubt that the Lenovo Googlebook 15 is meant for productivity and users of full-fledged MacBooks and Windows laptops, so we’d expect pricing to be in the same range, with the larger memory and storage configurations costing more.

title: GTA 5 Mod Adds Flock Surveillance Cameras So Players Can Blow Them Up
snippet: Built to highlight real-life surveillance, the mod includes 235 virtual cameras that you can destroy for in-game cash.
fullText:
Flock automated license plate-reading cameras are rapidly popping up all over the US. In some areas, they’re also going down pretty quick, too. 

Widespread opposition to Flock surveillance cameras has highlighted their inaccuracies and potential for abuse by authorities. A movement to “deflock” cities includes everything from canceling municipal contracts to covering cameras with trash bags and various forms of physical vandalism. 

Now, if you’re cruising through the fictional town of Los Santos (modeled after Los Angeles) in a new Grand Theft Auto 5 “mod,” you could be tracked by any of the 235 Flock cameras there. But you can also cash in $600 for each one you shoot down. 

The mod (a custom addition to the game) is called Grand Theft Automated License Plate Reader. Morry Kolman, the mod’s creator, said the in-game Flock cameras are based on “custom-built” 3D models, which subject players to “seemingly inescapable surveillance.”

Almost like living amid Big Brother, these virtual cameras take pictures of you and track your movements. If you commit crimes in the game — like speeding or hitting pedestrians — the cameras will report you to the police. They’ll even occasionally file “false reports” on you, just like the real cameras sometimes do. Players can also save the images captured by the cameras for use in social media posts or as wallpapers. 

And, because it’s Grand Theft Auto, you’re also allowed to fight back against the surveillance state, with access to weapons (like rocket launchers) that help you destroy the cameras. Once you’ve carried out an effective deflocking, you can pick up the mutilated remains and grab an in-game reward of $600 (the estimated value of the camera’s internal components based on a teardown conducted by Eyes Off Cedar Rapids). There’s also an integrated timer to keep track of how fast you deflock, allowing you to beat your PB.

A virtual protest

Cameras you destroy give you $600, based on the cost of parts for a real Flock camera.WTTDOTM

GTA 5 is chock-full of social commentary, from the dangers of consumerism to subtle critiques of extreme gamer behavior in characters like Trevor and Jimmy. The new Grand Theft Automated License Plate Reader mod builds on the general hatred toward and distrust of the massive Flock surveillance network adorning US roadways.

For some, it’s probably a fun (and less punitive) way to tap into unfulfilled vigilantism. But, according to Kolman, it also makes the game more difficult. “Not only does police surveillance become nearly impossible to evade, but representing Flock’s own history of inaccurate reporting, every time a player passes through a camera’s field of view, the mod creates a 1 in 20 chance that the ALPR will trigger a police chase without any cause,” according to the mod’s download page. 

In many ways, the new mod is a reality check for real-world privacy. If having 235 cameras follow you around in GTA feels like an oppressive nightmare in a claustrophobic game world, just remember that the real Los Angeles County has more than 10 times that amount.
excerpt:
Flock automated license plate-reading cameras are rapidly popping up all over the US. In some areas, they’re also going down pretty quick, too.

Widespread opposition to Flock surveillance cameras has highlighted their inaccuracies and potential for abuse by authorities. A movement to “deflock” cities includes everything from canceling municipal contracts to covering cameras with trash bags and various forms of physical vandalism.

title: Hands-on: Nothing’s $25 CMF Buds Neo are way better than the price suggests
snippet: Last month, Nothing’s CMF brand launched a new pair of $25 earbuds in the CMF Buds Neo. Too good to be true, I figured, but after getting my hands on them, I’m pleasantly surprised by what they bring to the table despite some expected downsides. more…
fullText:
Last month, Nothing’s CMF brand launched a new pair of $25 earbuds in the CMF Buds Neo. Too good to be true, I figured, but after getting my hands on them, I’m pleasantly surprised by what they bring to the table despite some expected downsides.

The CMF Buds Neo bring a lot to the table on paper. 52-hour battery life, active noise cancellation, some flashy colors, and even dual-device connections alongside support for the Nothing X app and EQ presets. For $25, it’s a compelling package. 

How does it deliver in real life?

I’ve spent a few hours listening to CMF Buds Neo and, honestly, I’m pretty impressed!

	

At their core, they get the job done. The earbuds have decent sound quality, though they’re a bit hollow on default settings. I found that turning down the bass enhancement improves the sound quality, and they’re more optimized for speech (podcasts, etc) than music. Nothing Ear (3a) sound far better; don’t get me wrong, but probably not 4x better as the price on paper suggests.

The sound quality is the most important thing here when the price is so low, and it’s certainly more than good enough to make these a good deal. And there’s clearly more weight put in the price than anything else. CMF Buds Neo have some clear and obvious downsides. The case is cheap-feeling despite looking very nice, and the same goes for the earbuds – the materials feel cheap, but they fit nice in my ear and stay comfortable over a few hours of use. The touchpads on the earbuds are responsive, but lack a play/pause gesture by default. Another downside is the range, as I found these disconnect from my Fold 8 more quickly than other earbuds I’ve tested in recent memory. The case magnets that hold the earbuds in place work well, and there are some nice touches such as a snappy hinge and the lanyard hole on a rotating corner piece. 

There’s also no pairing button on the case, something that will never fail to annoy me, but at least there’s Google Fast Pair – humorously, the Fast Pair pop-up lacks a picture of the earbuds and just says “blue” on the variant I bought.

Downsides are aplenty here, which really shouldn’t come as a surprise. But, at the core, you’re getting earbuds that sound good enough, have most important features, and cost just $25. If you need a spare pair of earbuds to throw in a backpack or at your bedside, or a daily driver on a budget, these are a winner in my book.

title: Gemini app makes Daily Brief free in the US
snippet: After introducing at I/O 2026 in May, Google is making Daily Brief in the Gemini app available for free in the US. more…
fullText:
After introducing at I/O 2026 in May, Google is making Daily Brief in the Gemini app available for free in the US.

Daily Brief generates a list of your to-dos and priorities every morning. Gemini uses Personal Intelligence to look at your Gmail, Google Calendar, and other Connected Apps, as well as past Gemini chats.

The Daily Brief starts with a “Top of mind” section that shows “timely, actionable items,” such as tasks with upcoming deadlines. “FYI” will show other items that have dates attached. “Looking ahead” is the final section with a focus on long-term goals and “suggested next steps to help you achieve them.”

You can tap on items to “Mark complete” or start a “Chat” with Gemini. There’s also the ability to leave “Helpful” or “Not helpful” feedback.

	

Example use cases include:

For students: Manage class schedules, organize study plans, and track applications.

For entrepreneurs: Surface actionable client emails and update task reminders.

For parents: Manage school communications, track family milestones, and handle household tasks.

For job seekers: Quickly act on recruiter inquiries, prepare for interviews, and monitor application statuses.

As of last Friday, Gemini Daily Brief no longer requires a Google AI subscription in the US. It’s available to personal Google Accounts with Personal Intelligence, Memory, and the Google Workspace integration enabled.

You can access it from the Gemini side panel, with Google also sending a notification every morning. You can disable that alert by going to the account menu and configuring “Notifications.” 

Another way to interact with the digest is through Gemini Live: “What’s my daily brief?”

title: This Is the Biggest 2D Map of the Universe. Here’s How to Use It
snippet: The map covers 75% of the sky, and you can explore all sorts of cool celestial objects once you know where to look.
fullText:
Scientists have pointed telescopes at the sky and mapped the cosmos for centuries. That relentless pursuit is producing maps that are bigger and more detailed than ever. But there’s one map that stands out above the rest, and now it’s the largest 2D map of the night sky ever created.

The best part? Anyone can play with it. 

The map, called Data Release 11 or DR11, comes courtesy of the DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys team, a collaborative effort between NSF NOIRLab, the Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, and other agencies and organizations.

Covering 75% of the sky across 5.6 trillion pixels, DR11 is the team’s most comprehensive map to date, built upon prior versions of the same map. It expands on DR9 by 50% and brings back northern sky coverage missing from DR10. Based on 263,407 ground-based exposures by 160 scientists, the map catalogs 4 billion objects — including stars, galaxies, black holes and asteroids — in visible and near-infrared light.

Already cited in over 1,800 research papers, researchers and collaborators expect this to remain the premier 2D map of its kind for years. According to co-lead David Schlegel, DR11 also helped identify 60 million targets for the DESI project and to build a full 3D map, which was completed in 2026, with future expansions planned. With billions of targets still unstudied, Schlegel told CNET that “plenty of other discoveries” remain hidden in plain sight for public exploration, and that DR11 is also being used to select additional targets for the 3D map.

Enough talk, let’s play

The map covers 75% of the night sky, with the black swath through the middle obscured by black holes, interstellar dust and other obstacles.Legacy Survey

The map doesn’t look like much at first. But if you pick a spot and start zooming in, you can get a pretty good idea of how vast it really is. What appears to be a cloud of pretty colors is actually billions of objects floating around in space.

You might notice that DR11, which is designed to see out into the universe, doesn’t contain any planets, moons or asteroids within our solar system. That may be a little bit of a bummer for some, but there are plenty of other objects to look for.

Though the user interface is a little overwhelming at first, you really only need four boxes to play around — and all four of them are right next to each other in the bottom-left corner. 

Zoom: This indicates how zoomed in you are based on the +/- slider on the top left. It goes from degrees to arc minutes and then finally to arc seconds. I got most of my best results between 20 and 50 arc minutes. 

Contrast and brightness: Below zoom, you’ll find the contrast slider, which reduces the background noise of the map. Under that, the brightness slider helps illuminate smaller objects. Adjust these settings as needed to get the best view, but start with the defaults.

Jump to object: This is the most important box, where you can type in the names of celestial bodies to find them on the map. I searched for a couple dozen celestial objects and found them all pretty quickly. Online lists of named black holes, quasars and other cool celestial bodies can be a good starting point in exploring the universe — I have more tips for finding them if you keep reading.  

Once you land on something, use the zoom slider in the top-left corner to zoom in and get a closer look. (Don’t use your mouse wheel for this because it zooms in wherever your pointer is, potentially taking you to a completely different part of the map.) You can also drag the cursor around the screen to view everything around the object you’re looking at.

A sky like you’ve never seen it

Arcturus is comparably huge in the night sky, and so it is also comparably huge on the map.Legacy Survey

My first visit on the map was to Arcturus, the fourth-largest star in the sky. Zoomed in, it’s much larger than every other object around it by a rather wide margin, which is why it’s so easy to find in the night sky. 

Another search took me to LHS 1140b, the first star ever discovered that sits in another star’s habitable zone with an atmosphere. This one is much smaller than Arcturus and required me to zoom in to 30 arc seconds to see it. It’s quite close to its host star, which makes sense since the habitable zone is pretty close to the star itself. Earth would appear at a similar distance from the sun if viewed from this perspective. 

The star that LHS 1140b orbits is also dimmer than many other stars. It’s about 20% the size of the sun, so it almost looks like a big planet rather than a small star.

This binary star system hosts planet HD 80606 b, a planet known to orbit so close to its star that it is scorched. It’s so close, in fact, that the light from the binary star system hides it completely.Legacy Survey

Some stuff is easier to find than others. For example, planet HD 80606 b is so close to its star that it is absolutely scorched, with temperature swings of 1,100 degrees Fahrenheit. Bright glare from its binary stars completely obscures HD 80606 b on the map. It’s still there, though, getting blasted by its star like a blowtorch caramelizing sugar on the top of a crème brûlée.

You’ll notice that the map has a large, sweeping blank spot running through it. These are the parts of the sky that haven’t been mapped yet. Researchers say that this is due to various obstacles, such as space dust, bright stars getting in the way of scans and black holes covering everything behind them. 

For example, try searching for Sagittarius A*, the supermassive black hole at the center of the Milky Way. The map shows you where it is — right inside one of those blank bands. The black hole prevents any telescope from seeing the stars and planets behind it, so that part of the map remains blank. 

More advanced options

The planet LHS 1140b orbits a star about one-fifth the size of our sun, and is one of the better candidates for a planet hosting life. Legacy Viewer

You’ll also see a box with a ton of options in the top-right corner of the map. For basic viewing, you don’t have to interact with this box at all, but there are some fun things in there if you want to see them. 

Images: This dropdown menu lets you select which set of images you want to use. Leave that on Legacy Surveys DR11 because that’s the most recent dataset. 

Overlays: This menu is more complicated, as it includes a lot of different datasets you can overlay. Many of them just show which telescopes, instruments and surveys found each separate part of the map. You can leave them all off and still search around the universe for cool stuff. 

However, there is one set of overlays that is worth your time: the Bright objects overlay, with options that actually help you navigate the map. For example, the Bright stars option will put blue circles around the brightest stars on the map with names, making them much easier to find. That’s how I learned that the designation for Arcturus is HR 5340.

Bright objects include star clusters, planetary nebulae and some more specific ones — but the most fun is the Constellations overlay, which shows off every constellation in the sky. If you toggle it on, pick a constellation and zoom into each corner and point, you can find the bright stars that humans used to construct these constellations ages ago. 

Finding stuff to search for

Constellations such as Ursa Minor can be seen on the 2D map, letting you explore the bright stars that make up their shape.Legacy Survey

The real challenge in using the DR11 app is figuring out what to look up. There are all sorts of celestial bodies, and many of them have some pretty cool stories. However, there really isn’t much of a repository to find these things.

We know AI isn’t great at many things, but Schlegel suggested that a large language model may be pretty good for this application since it can scan the web quickly. 

This isn’t without its caveats. Schlegel said that Google Gemini tends to “spit out sexagesimal coordinates” that don’t work in the map’s viewer website because they’re an archaic sky-mapping system. However, Anthropic’s Claude uses decimal-degree coordinates, which work. While the team is looking into supporting both, Schlegel said he prefers the newer decimal system over the archaic system originally invented by Hipparchus and Ptolemy.

The team also gave CNET a list of some pretty neat stuff to look up in the map viewer if you need more ideas. These are some of the most gorgeous pieces of imagery on the entire map: 

NGC 5272 – The Globular Cluster

NGC 4826 – The Black Eye Galaxy

NGC 3351 – The Barred Spiral Galaxy

NGC 4486 – Virgo A

NGC 5457 – The Pinwheel Galaxy

NGC 4594 – Sombrero Galaxy

Schlegel also recommended visiting an FAQ web page for more granular guidance on using the search and overlay functions to improve your experience.
excerpt:
Scientists have pointed telescopes at the sky and mapped the cosmos for centuries. That relentless pursuit is producing maps that are bigger and more detailed than ever. But there’s one map that stands out above the rest, and now it’s the largest 2D map of the night sky ever created.

The best part? Anyone can play with it.

title: Apple iPhone 18 Pro Max vs. Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra: The Highest-End Phones Compared
snippet: The iPhone 18 Pro Max has a big camera upgrade – and a bigger price. How does it compare to Samsung’s flagship phone?
fullText:
Apple’s $1,299 iPhone 18 Pro Max now stands tall as the company’s newest nonfolding high-end flagship phone. Announced at the company’s Surprise and Shine event on Wednesday, it packs big camera and battery upgrades. But with a starting price that’s $100 higher than the iPhone 17 Pro Max, the phone’s 256GB model is now priced closely to Samsung’s $1,300 Galaxy S26 Ultra.

While every iPhone received a $100 price increase that’s likely influenced by the ongoing RAM shortage, Apple’s topline iPhone appears to be a close rival to the S26 Ultra in several key areas, especially when it comes to battery life and cameras.

The Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra.

Andrew Lanxon/CNET

iPhone 18 Pro Max vs. Galaxy S26 Ultra design and display

While Apple’s iPhone 18 Pro Max and Samsung’s Galaxy S26 Ultra are big phones, their design aesthetics are quite different. The 18 Pro Max sports a similar aluminum unibody design to the one that debuted on last year’s 17 Pro Max. It comes in burgundy red, glacier blue, silver and black colors. Its shape gives it a hefty appearance, but one that fits in well when the phone is being used as a professional camera for events like Apple TV’s Major League Baseball broadcasts. And at 249 grams (8.8 ounces), the 18 Pro Max isn’t lightweight by any stretch. The phone has a 6.8-inch OLED display that should be quite expansive for videos, websites and games.

The Galaxy S26 Ultra has a slightly bigger 6.9-inch AMOLED display, but at 214 grams, it’s notably lighter than the iPhone 18 Pro Max. It also comes in six colors: pink gold, silver shadow, cobalt violet, sky blue, white and black. The S26 Ultra is also the thinnest in its line, but its Privacy Display is its most unique feature. The S26 Ultra’s display can make specific apps or notifications difficult to see from off-angle viewing, making it easier to hide content from prying eyes without needing to apply a privacy screen protector. No other company has replicated Samsung’s Privacy Display, which does make the phone stand out.

The iPhone 18 Pro Max in glacier blue.Apple/CNET

iPhone 18 Pro Max vs. Galaxy S26 Ultra battery capacity

Both phones have big batteries. While Apple doesn’t disclose its battery specs in the US — instead citing that it can play 45 hours of video — its Ireland website claims the physical SIM edition will have a 5,391-mAh capacity. That’s slightly higher than the 5,000-mAh capacity on the S26 Ultra and might be even higher on the eSIM model that will be sold in the US.

Apple hasn’t yet disclosed the charging speed for the iPhone 18 Pro Max, but this is an area where Samsung already excels — the S26 Ultra has 60-watt wired charging and won our CNET Lab Test award for fastest wired charging phone by recharging from 0% to 76% in 30 minutes. That said, last year’s iPhone 17 Pro Max had a 40-watt charging speed that was one of our top performers, recharging 0% to 69% in the same 30-minute test. We look forward to testing out the 18 Pro Max to see how it fares.

You can turn on Privacy Display in Quick Settings to prevent others from seeing what’s on your screen.

Celso Bulgatti/CNET

Both phones also have their respective companies’ highest-end cameras, with Apple’s iPhone 18 Pro Max now featuring a variable-aperture camera that can physically open or close to take better photos in darker or lighter environments. This feature comes with the Pro Max’s three-camera setup that includes a 49-megapixel wide camera, a 48-megapixel ultrawide camera and a 48-megapixel telephoto camera with a 4x optical zoom. While the S26 Ultra doesn’t include a variable aperture, it has four cameras on the back that include a 200-megapixel main camera, a 50-megapixel ultrawide, a 50-megapixel telephoto with a 5x optical zoom and a 10-megapixel telephoto with a 3x optical zoom. 

	

			

iPhone 18 Pro Max vs. Galaxy S26 Ultra processor, features

Apple’s A20 Pro processor powers the company’s latest AI features, headlined by the new Siri AI assistant that is built with Apple’s collaboration with Google’s Gemini. It can help you look up specific information buried in your emails and texts and turn them into actionable items like new reminders or calendar events. Apple also made a point of showing off the A20 Pro’s gaming abilities and how the phone’s vapor chamber helps keep it running cool while pushing intensive graphics. 

But Samsung’s phone includes Qualcomm’s Snapdragon 8 Gen 5 for Galaxy processor, powering its own slate of Galaxy AI features focused on proactive suggestions, along with photo editing. It’s also quite capable of high-end gaming.

Apple’s major new software updates for iPhone, iPad, Mac, and more are almost here.

iOS 27, iPadOS 27, macOS Golden Gate, watchOS 27, tvOS 27, and visionOS 27 will ship to all users next week on Monday, September 14.

After a full summer of beta testing, today Apple is rolling out the RC versions of those updates.

title: Google’s hyper-personalized ‘Dreambeans’ feed is now free to test [U]
snippet: Dreambeans is an experimental app from Google Labs that will “proactively dream up personalized daily stories.” After previously requiring a subscription, Dreambeans is now available for free Google Accounts in the US to test. more…
fullText:
Dreambeans is an experimental app from Google Labs that will “proactively dream up personalized daily stories.” After previously requiring a subscription, Dreambeans is now available for free Google Accounts in the US to test.

Update 9/10: Google officially announced the broader availability today.

Personalized topics: This could be everything from places to explore, shows to watch, or a reminder of upcoming events.

Connected apps: Distilled information from the Google apps you select, including Calendar, Gmail, Photos, Search, YouTube, and now Gemini.

Original 8/28: Dreambeans is very much like a hyper-personalized Google Now or Discover feed. Like the Gemini app and AI Mode, it uses Google’s Personal Intelligence system to learn your interests by looking at your Gmail, Google Photos, Calendar, Workspace, Search history, and YouTube. During setup, you can choose which apps Dreambeans can access.

Workspace supplies ground-truth transaction data like receipts and upcoming flights

Photos provides the visual memories and insights about you and the people in your life

YouTube identifies your active hobbies

Search detects your budding interests

By combining all these unique signals, Dreambeans can proactively generate rich and highly customized daily visual stories.

The app suggests topics to explore, things to try, places to visit, and interesting events. New stories arrive every morning.

	

Instead of using stock imagery, each Dreambeans story is accompanied by Nano Banana 2-generated artwork that uses an illustrated style. For example, if Dreambeans recommends a hike, you might see yourself and a group of friends at that location.

Tapping on a story lets you see a longer description. In the same example, you’ll get trail details, specific places to stop, what to wear, and timing recommendations. Dreambeans will link to trail guide content on the web. There’s also an “Ask anything” chat experience to get more information.

You can leave feedback by tapping the heart or downvoting, while the chat interface allows you to provide more details. “Tune your feed” lets you tell Dreambeans what you “want more stories about” and what it should never show.

The name combines two ideas at the heart of the app. The “dream” is how the app works overnight to find meaning in the content overload across your connected apps. It then distills what it finds into “beans” – a fresh collection of stories brewed for you each morning.

In June, it was just available for Google AI Ultra subscribers, with Google expanding to AI Pro earlier this month. The setup process “requires up to a day to build your first set of stories.” 

It remains to be seen how Dreambeans will graduate from Google Labs. The experience it offers today is largely standalone, with Daily Brief in the Gemini app possibly benefiting from a more visual experience. 

Dreambeans is available on Android and iOS in the US.

fullText:
Look, no offense to Apple Vision Pro. I’m sure Apple Vision Pro is a very nice person. But iPhone Duo and Apple Vision Pro are not the same.

There’s a take that the iPhone Duo may have the Apple Vision Pro problem. The idea is that due to its price and device-specific software, it may be a miss and not a hit.  The two things are not the same.

iPhone Duo doesn’t suffer from Apple Vision Pro’s biggest challenges

The biggest problem with this view is that Apple Vision Pro doesn’t replace core devices. It can be a portable movie theater and a better viewport into gaming, and mixed reality experiences can be really moving.

Apple Vision Pro doesn’t replace your iPhone or your iPad. It’s an immersive world that can fit in a suitcase. Apple Vision Pro is mostly a stationary appliance. It’s not a small tablet that can fit in your pocket that you’ll use literally everywhere you go.

Then there’s price. iPhone Duo’s $1999 starting price is a lot, but it’s not as bad as we’d feared. People are willing to pay for premium smartphones. That’s just a result of how important phones are to modern life. 

Apple Vision Pro’s original $3,499 starting price was never very palatable. Now it starts at $3,699. You can almost buy two iPhone Duos. That’s iPhone Quattro money. 

Utility, portability, and affordability all feed into the biggest difference. Apple Vision Pro fails as a mainstream consumer product for all of these reasons. As a result, it struggles to fully realize its potential.

iPhone Duo is both an iPhone and a small iPad

iPhone Duo has the utility of an iPhone and a small iPad in a form factor that can fit in your pocket. It’s also the same price as say, buying an iPhone 16 Pro one year and upgrading to the iPhone 17 Pro the next year. That’s not unheard of.

Sure, iPhone Duo will have an uphill battle with software optimization, at least for third-party apps. But Apple has already crafted a highly considered story around the operating system and first-party apps. Developers will soon have the tools to make great apps for the versatile folding display as well.

The biggest challenge with the iPhone Duo, to me, is that it’s not the absolute best-in-class iPhone yet. Hopefully it can be in some future version.

	

It would be great to have the best of every iPhone in one device, including the foldable display. But for now, the iPhone 18 Pro still wins in the camera department and Face ID.

Importantly, those trade-offs won’t be missed for consumers curious to try a radically new iPhone form factor. 

In the kindest way possible, Apple Vision Pro wishes it had iPhone Duo’s challenges.
